entries.subject: Celestia native nucleus illustration and catalog scale
entries.finding: Superseded 2026-09-16: the Celestia generic mesh was a shared illustration with no relation to this nucleus, and its catalogue radius was an estimate. The package now shows a smooth ellipsoid at the published effective radius (Snodgrass, Lowry and Fitzsimmons (2006), MNRAS 373, 1590); no mesh from Celestia is retained.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured shape model of this nucleus (radar, spacecraft or a convex lightcurve inversion with a stated pole) would replace the ellipsoid.

entries.subject: Published event and observation context
entries.finding: Retained intake decision: Holmes became about a million times brighter during its 2007 outburst. The expanding dust cloud was enormous compared with the small nucleus that released it. The cited material supplies explanatory context; it does not qualify photographic terrain on this nucleus.

entries.subject: Published effective nucleus radius
entries.finding: Snodgrass, Lowry and Fitzsimmons (2006), MNRAS 373, 1590: effective radius 1.62 km ± 0.01. Lightcurves give an axis ratio of at least 1.3, used here as the displayed elongation, with a period between 7.2 and 12.8 hours. Used as the volume-equivalent radius of the displayed ellipsoid.
